blocks.text: The National Arts Festival in Makhanda, South Africa, invites applications for an Artistic Director to lead its curatorial vision, champion emerging talent and strengthen artistic exchange across Africa and internationally. The position is offered on a five-year renewable contract.
Open Call:

The National Arts Festival (NAF) is recruiting an Artistic Director to shape the next chapter of one of South Africa’s established multidisciplinary arts festivals. The successful candidate will define the festival’s artistic vision, curatorial identity, and long-term programming strategy, positioning Makhanda as a centre for contemporary African artistic production, experimentation, and exchange. Working alongside the Chief Executive Officer, the Artistic Director will oversee artistic programming, commissioning, artist relationships, the Fringe programme, emerging artist development and international partnerships.

The role encompasses theatre, dance, music, comedy, visual arts, literature, film, digital arts and interdisciplinary practices, with an emphasis on artistic quality, cultural representation and innovation. A central responsibility will be developing new opportunities for African artists through commissions, mentorship, touring pathways and collaborations with festivals across the continent and internationally.
Institutional Context:

The National Arts Festival is a multidisciplinary cultural event held annually in Makhanda, South Africa. With a history spanning more than five decades, the festival brings together established and emerging artists working across diverse disciplines and cultural traditions. Its programming includes curated performances and exhibitions, the Fringe platform, artist development initiatives and opportunities for international cultural exchange.

The appointment supports the festival’s ambition to strengthen its position as a leading contemporary African arts festival over the next 50 years. The Artistic Director will contribute to this development by supporting new artistic production, expanding international networks and strengthening connections between the festival, its audiences and the wider cultural sector.
Eligibility and Criteria:
The festival seeks a highly networked artistic leader who can develop a distinctive curatorial vision and manage a complex multidisciplinary programme.
Applicants should demonstrate:
The ability to develop and implement a long-term artistic and curatorial strategy.
Knowledge of contemporary African artistic practices across multiple disciplines.
Strong relationships with artists, curators, cultural organisations and international networks.
Experience managing substantial budgets and taking responsibility for expenditure.
The ability to work independently and meet demanding deadlines.
Strong communication, consultation and leadership skills.
Resourcefulness in working within financial constraints.
The ability to identify partnerships and contribute to fundraising activities.
The successful candidate will also be expected to advance cultural, linguistic and demographic representation, support indigenous African artistic forms and engage with emerging technologies.
Experience in artistic commissioning, artist development, international collaboration and multidisciplinary programming will be particularly relevant to the position.
Evaluation Process:

The Artistic Director will report directly to the Chief Executive Officer and form part of the festival’s executive leadership. The role includes chairing an Artistic Committee comprising practising artists, curators and sector specialists who advise on programming, artistic recognition and quality standards.

The National Arts Festival’s Board provides strategic oversight through the Chief Executive Officer and its Artistic Programming subcommittee. Applicants should consult the full Terms of Reference for additional information.
The festival’s recruitment process is guided by its Employment Equity commitments and aims to ensure its team reflects South Africa’s diversity.
Practical Information:
Application deadline : 30 October 2026
Position: Artistic Director
Institution: National Arts Festival
Location: Makhanda, Eastern Cape, South Africa
Contract: Five-year renewable term
Reporting line: Chief Executive Officer
The appointed Artistic Director will lead the festival’s artistic programme, including its Fringe, Young Artists, and new commissioning initiatives.

Responsibilities will also include developing an NAF New Works programme, strengthening opportunities for artists to tour nationally and internationally, and contributing to an Artist Development Fund.

The role further involves collaboration with Makhanda stakeholders, including Rhodes University, on year-round creative programming, alongside initiatives to engage younger audiences and activate the festival’s archive.
Applications and Queries:
Submit applications exclusively through the National Arts Festival’s official online application form.
Applications submitted by email or through other channels will not be considered.
Applicants are encouraged to review the full Terms of Reference before submitting their applications.
